rv.q: Happily, though, American Blues Theater’s production of “Always … Patsy Cline,” Ted Swindley’s warhorse of a revue that premiered in 1988, largely won me over with the warmth of its two leading ladies — Liz Chidester and Molly Hernández — and its tender portrayal of their unexpected friendship.
American Blues Theater has done it again with Always…Patsy Cline, running now through June 21st.
The pair of talented actors/singers in this two-person tribute to Patsy Cline are equally sensational.
Always . . . Patsy Cline is a stellar example of the magic that ensues when the director brings out the very best in her cast.
Always…Patsy Cline hits every banger in her juke box for a sonically charged good time that will make you want to leave your seat and Texas two-step down the aisle.
The show is worth seeing just to hear that instrument of hers in action, reminding us why Patsy Cline and the Nashville sound in general remains such a force in American pop culture.
You'd be 'Crazy' not to see this warm, wonderful show...
Despite this possible flaw and some superficialities, the advantage of this show is its lightheartedness in the face of the two characters' personal tragedies.
